evidence: All ~40 language run.sh files share an identical structural skeleton: (1) set -e, (2) emoji + language header echo, (3) 'check if runtime installed' block with same error message template, (4) version echo, (5) 'Running X active inference simulation...' echo, (6) tool invocation, (7) success echo. The only variation is the language name, tool names, and invocation command.

run_all.sh line 177: comment '# Make all run.sh scripts executable' immediately above the find/chmod line — the comment restates the command rather than explaining why it is done at this point (e.g. in case CI checks out without exec bits).

status_dashboard.sh lines 127-139: language category counts are computed by running `echo '<space-separated list>' | wc -w` on inline string literals that duplicate the exact category lists defined in show_implementations() at lines 160-167. The duplication is never exercised by a shared data source.

status_dashboard.sh main() at lines 265-278 is a pure dispatcher calling six show_* functions sequentially with no conditional logic, transformation, or error handling — a textbook pass-through orchestrator with no added value beyond sequence.

Active_Shellference.sh: comment '# Execute the simulation' (line 183) above the single call `run_simulation` echoes the function name without adding context. Similarly '# Define global variables' (line 17) above three declare statements re-states what the code obviously does.

Active_Shellference.sh: ERROR messages use generic capitalized prefix 'ERROR:' with mechanical location strings ('KL divergence computation failed at index $i', 'EFE inner computation failed at [$i,$j]', 'EFE outer computation failed at state $i') — these are structurally identical boilerplate blocks copy-pasted across calculate_kl_divergence and calculate_efe.

Shell/run.sh generates a default config.sh inline if absent, duplicating the CONFIG_* variable names and values from the actual config.sh that already exists in the same directory — a defensive fallback that is unreachable in practice if the repository is checked out intact.

status_dashboard.sh show_system_info(): comment '# OS Information', '# CPU Information', '# Memory Information', '# Available languages/compilers' all restate section headings that match the echo strings immediately below them.

strengths: Active_Shellference.sh function comments accurately describe the algorithm (KL divergence formula, Bayes update normalization, EFE minimization) — these explain WHY and WHAT the math does, not just echoing the code.
The sentinel comment in select_action ('# Sentinel: larger than any realistic EFE for this simulation') adds genuine reasoning for the magic number 1000000.
config.sh validate_config() provides real defensive checks at a genuine configuration boundary (probability sums, range validation) — not defensive overengineering.
run_all.sh parallel/sequential mode branching and argument parsing is purposeful scaffolding, not mere boilerplate.
Shell/run.sh correctly notes WHY it must use scalar export format for Active_Shellference.sh compatibility — a comment that explains a non-obvious constraint.
ai_generated_debt.issue_character: The dominant AI-generated debt pattern is structural template cloning: every language run.sh is the same boilerplate skeleton with variable substitution, and status_dashboard.sh duplicates category data instead of sourcing it from run_all.sh's LANGUAGES array, with restating section-header comments throughout.
ai_generated_debt.score_rationale: The codebase sits below the midpoint for ai_generated_debt cleanliness. The ~40 language runner scripts are near-identical boilerplate that a template or single parameterized function could replace, and status_dashboard.sh duplicates category membership data instead of deriving it from the authoritative LANGUAGES array. The core simulation logic in Active_Shellference.sh is relatively clean with purposeful comments, which prevents a lower score, but the pervasive structural copy-paste across the runner layer is a clear LLM-hallmark pattern that a developer would need to audit before extending the codebase.

issues.summary: All ~40 language run.sh files are structural clones of one template with only tool names changed
evidence: Ada/run.sh and Golang/run.sh share identical structure: set -e, header echo, 'if ! command -v <tool>', 'echo ✅ <Lang> found: $(<tool> --version)', 'echo 🔨 Compiling/Building...', invocation, 'echo ✅ <Lang> simulation completed successfully!'
The only non-template variation across files is the tool name, compile command, and binary name — no file adds auth, logging, metrics, or retry logic that would justify the duplication
issues.suggestion: Extract a shared run_language_impl.sh helper that accepts tool_name, check_cmd, version_cmd, build_cmd, run_cmd as parameters, or parameterize via a simple dispatch table in run_all.sh so each language entry is a data record rather than a script copy.

issues.summary: status_dashboard.sh redefines language category lists independently from run_all.sh's authoritative LANGUAGES array
evidence: run_all.sh lines 21-62 define the LANGUAGES array as the authoritative list of 40 languages
status_dashboard.sh lines 127-139 compute category counts by running wc -w on hardcoded inline string literals
status_dashboard.sh lines 159-168 define a separate categories associative array with the same language/directory mappings, again duplicated from run_all.sh
issues.suggestion: Source run_all.sh or extract a shared data file (e.g. languages.sh) that both scripts source, so category membership has one authoritative definition.

issues.summary: status_dashboard.sh section header comments restate echo strings rather than adding context
evidence: Line 77: '# OS Information' immediately above 'echo -e "  🖥️  OS: ..."' — redundant
Line 84: '# CPU Information' above the nproc block — redundant
Line 88: '# Memory Information' above the free block — redundant
Line 95: '# Available languages/compilers' above the tools array — redundant
Active_Shellference.sh line 17: '# Define global variables' above three declare statements
issues.suggestion: Remove comments that merely restate what the adjacent code obviously does. Keep only comments that explain non-obvious constraints (e.g. why lsb_release vs /etc/os-release fallback).

issues.summary: Shell/run.sh generates a default config.sh that duplicates values from the already-present config.sh
evidence: Shell/run.sh lines 22-38: 'if [ ! -f config.sh ]' block generates a config with different CONFIG_TRANSITION_PROBS and CONFIG_PRECISION values than config.sh, and a no-op validate_config stub

config.sh already exists in the repository at Shell/config.sh with validated parameters; the fallback path is unreachable in a checked-out repo and silently uses different parameter values if ever triggered
issues.suggestion: Remove the inline config generation fallback; instead emit an error directing the user to copy the provided config.sh template, so parameter divergence is not silently introduced.

root_causes: Template-driven generation: the codebase appears to have been produced by applying a single LLM prompt per language with variable substitution, resulting in structurally identical scripts rather than data-parameterized runners
Lack of DRY enforcement at the orchestration layer: run_all.sh and status_dashboard.sh evolved as separate artifacts rather than sharing a common data source for language/category metadata
possible_false_positives: restating_section_comments: some section headers in show_system_info may be retained for readability in a dashboard-style script where visual grouping has user value
